claims.text: Because Search placement restricts delivery to search results and related Pins, a useful conditional signal is search-placement share of impressions and clicks: if search-only ad groups capture a meaningful share of delivery versus browse-only ad groups, that suggests your keywords or targeting align with active search demand. The trade-off is that narrowing to Search reduces total potential reach compared with the default All placement, so volume may drop even if relevance rises.

claims.text: Pinterest publishes no vendor-reported performance or uplift figures for Search placement, so no guaranteed outcomes can be stated.

relationships.name: Facebook Search Results placement
relationships.difference: Meta's Facebook Search Results placement is a selectable placement option specifically for image ads, per the Meta ads guide; Pinterest's Search placement is an ad group placement option (Search, Browse, or All) available in Ads Manager and Bulk Editor and covers search results and related Pins.
relationships.context: Both place ads in search results on their respective platforms, but Meta's option is documented for image ads while Pinterest's is a general ad group placement setting.

evidence.locator: Choose your ad placement: 'Facebook search results'

relationships.name: Search campaigns
relationships.difference: Google Search campaigns are a whole campaign type that places ads across Google's network of search results, with its own campaign creation flow (objective, campaign type, ad groups, ads, budget); Pinterest's Search placement is a placement option within a Pinterest ad group, not a separate campaign type.
relationships.context: Both reach people searching, but Google's is a campaign-level construct on Google's search network while Pinterest's is a placement toggle inside Pinterest campaign setup.

evidence.locator: Under “Select a campaign type” select Search

relationships.name: Discover placement (Demand Gen)
relationships.difference: Google's Discover is a channel placement selectable in Demand Gen manual channel selection, serving ads in the Discover feed; Pinterest's Search placement serves ads in search results and related Pins, not a feed-style discovery surface.
relationships.context: Both are placement/channel selections within their platforms' campaign setup, but they target different surfaces (Discover feed vs Pinterest search results).

evidence.locator: Manual channel selection list: "Discover"

relationships.name: Gmail placement (Demand Gen)
relationships.difference: Google's Gmail placement is a channel placement in Demand Gen manual channel selection serving ads in Gmail; Pinterest's Search placement serves ads in Pinterest search results and related Pins.
relationships.context: Both are selectable placements within campaign setup, but on entirely different surfaces (Gmail inbox vs Pinterest search).

evidence.locator: Manual channel selection list: "Gmail"

relationships.name: Automatic placement
relationships.difference: TikTok's Automatic placement is set by default for Smart+ ad groups, with placements selected automatically unless the advertiser switches to Select placement; Pinterest's default is All placements (Search and Browse), and the advertiser explicitly chooses Search, Browse, or All.
relationships.context: Both involve placement selection defaults in ad group setup, but TikTok's is an automatic system selection within Smart+ while Pinterest's is a manual choice among named placements.

evidence.locator: Automatic placement is set by default

relationships.name: Placement exclusions
relationships.difference: Google's placement exclusions stop ads serving on specific pages, sites, mobile apps, and videos (account-level and MCC-level, respected by Performance Max); Pinterest's Search placement is a positive placement selection, not an exclusion control.
relationships.context: Both concern where ads can serve, but exclusions are a negative control list while Pinterest's Search placement is a positive targeting choice.

evidence.locator: "Performance Max campaigns will respect all account-level and MCC-level placement exclusions."
